summary: Annemarie Schimmel worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. She earned doctorates at Humboldt University and Marburg, studying under Hans Heinrich Schaeder and Friedrich Heiler. Her career included professorships at Marburg, Ankara, Bonn, and Harvard (1967–1992).

Annemarie von Gabain worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Humboldt University (PhD) and Peking University, she held posts at Ankara University (1935–1937), Humboldt University (1939–1945), and the University of Hamburg (1949–1966).

Philosopher Annette Baier studied at the University of Otago and Somerville College (PhD 1952). She held faculty posts at Carnegie Mellon University (~1968–1973) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1973–1995).

Annette L. Heitmann works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Christian Lindtner and David Seyfort Ruegg, attending the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989) and earning a doctoral degree from the University of Vienna (completed by 2002).

Indologist and historian Annette Schmiedchen earned her PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin and completed her habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. Her career includes posts at Halle-Wittenberg and Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 2021).

Annette Susannah Beveridge worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her studies at Bedford College, London, attending from around 1858 to 1860 and from 1862 to 1867.
Annette Wilke works in Indology and religious studies. She held academic posts at the University of Bern (~1993–1998) and the University of Münster (~1998–2019).
Annie Barber Clarke was an Indology scholar who studied at Radcliffe College (1883–1886) under Charles Rockwell Lanman. She later held teaching positions at Parsons School and Miss Brown's School.

Linguist and Indologist Annie Montaut studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Paris Cité, and Paris Nanterre. She held teaching posts at Tunis, Queen's University, Jawaharlal Nehru University (1981–1987), Paris Nanterre (1987–1990), and served on INALCO's editorial board (1990–2014).

Anshul Agarwal works in computational studies and Indology. Agarwal earned a Bachelor of Engineering from Vivekanand Education Society's Institute of Technology in 2014 and held a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur.

Antanas Poška was an Indologist and historian who studied at Vytautas Magnus University (1926–1929), earned a B.A. from the University of Mumbai (1931–1933), and pursued doctoral studies at the University of Calcutta (~1931–1936).

Anthony C. Yu worked in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (PhD), where he taught from around 1968 to 2005 as a professor in the humanities and divinity school.

Anthony Cerulli specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Loyola, Yale, and the University of Chicago (PhD 2007). He held posts at Loyola, Transylvania University, Hobart and William Smith Colleges (2008–2016), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2016–2021).

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a scholar of Sinology and history. He studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak, whom he later succeeded, serving at Leiden as a lecturer from 1946 and as professor from 1956 to 1975.
Anthony Good is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held an appointment at the University of Edinburgh as Professor Emeritus (attested 2000, 2026).

Anthony Hendrik Nicolaas Verwey worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University, and held a post at the National Museum of Ethnology from 1947 to 1981.

Anthony J. Alston worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Hari Prasad Shastri (~1946–1956) and earned his PhD at Banaras Hindu University (~1959–1964) under the supervision of T. R. V. Murti.

Anthony Kennedy Warder specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at SOAS under John Brough and William Stede, later serving as Lecturer at the University of Edinburgh (1955–1963) and department chair at the University of Toronto (1963–1990).

Anthony Tribe works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bristol and Oxford (DPhil 1995 under Alexis Sanderson), with additional instruction from Paul Williams and Steven Collins. He held posts at the University of Montana (1997) and University of Arizona (2020).

Anthony W. Barber specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1984 and later held a post at the University of Calgary (attested 1998).
